title: Framewise prefetch + tool-hedge SDK PRD (draft)
content:
Purpose
This PRD captures a proposal for a latency-first "framewise prefetch" protocol combined with a 'tool hedging' policy and concise typed partial JSON profiles for the Hosted API. The focus is to reduce tail latency for hybrid generation+tool workflows (where the model issues tool calls mid-stream) while preserving structured output guarantees and offering ergonomic client SDKs for incremental consumption, resume, and client-side hedging.

Why this problem matters
- Increasing number of real customer flows interleave generation and external tools (retrieval, calculator, external APIs). Current hosted streaming patterns either block on tool resolution or emit low-fidelity placeholders that complicate client logic.
- Tail latency and jitter during tool resolution create poor interactive UX (spinner times > 500ms and intermittent stalls).
- Developers want a simple SDK contract: incremental deterministic frames, clear semantics for partial/complete JSON output, and built-in patterns for speculative local hedging to reduce perceived latency.

Goals & success metrics (90 days)
- UX latency: reduce median perceived time-to-first-meaningful-token for tool-involving sessions by 30%.
- Tail latency: 95th percentile stall time during tool calls reduced by 40% for instrumented customers.
- Developer ergonomics: SDK telemetry shows 80% of instrumented clients adopt a single-frame-consumption path within 6 weeks of launch.
- Correctness: structured output parse success rate across existing prompt suites >= 99.5% after rollout.

Non-goals
- This is not a full replacement for existing full-session resume semantics. We avoid changing session persistence semantics beyond frame resume tokens.
- Not addressing complex multi-agent tool orchestration (that belongs to orchestration product).

User stories
1) As a product engineer building a chat assistant, I want the client SDK to show incremental partial answers while a retrieval tool runs, without risking inconsistent JSON output or confusing UI flashes.
2) As an SDK integrator, I want a single API for streaming frames, resume tokens, and a small set of hedging helpers so I don’t invent ad-hoc speculative local completions.
3) As an SRE/ops user, I want telemetry hooks that show when hedged fallbacks were used and their success rates so we can tune server-side routing and prefetch thresholds.

High-level design
- Framewise prefetch protocol: server emits incremental "frames" (compact partial outputs) delimited by stable tokens. Each frame includes: a sequence id, optional resume_token, typed payload ("narrative", "action_call", "patch"), and a short confidence hint. Frames are designed to be small (target < 2KB) to encourage early UI updates.
- Tool hedging policy: when the model emits a tool call frame, the platform will simultaneously: (A) begin routing the tool request to configured tool endpoints, and (B) optionally return a speculative soft-output frame that contains a lightweight best-effort fallback summary and a hedging token indicating it is speculative. The SDK exposes helpers to display speculative content differently and to reconcile when a concrete tool response arrives.
- Typed partial JSON profiles: frames carry typed schema hints (simple JSON-LD-like tags) so clients can incrementally validate/merge structured output. A final commit frame indicates the authoritative final structure.

API sketch (hosted API additions)
- New streaming frame envelope (HTTP SSE / websocket / event frames):
  event: frame
  data: {"seq": "int", "type": "string", "payload": "string(base64 or escaped)", "resume_token": "str?", "speculative": "bool", "schema_tag": "str?", "confidence": "float?"}
- Shortcut: For non-streaming users, a synchronous response may include a final commit object and a 'frames' list with the last N frames for debugging.

Frame types (examples)
- narrative: partial free-text tokens (non-actionable).
- action_call: structured tool invocation {tool: string, args: {...}} emitted as its own frame; includes resume_token to allow later resume.
- tool_patch: small structured merge indicating tool result fields that should be merged into the final object (patch semantics).
- commit: final authoritative object with version id.

SDK Ergonomics (JS/Types)
- Simple consumer API:
  const stream = client.stream({model, prompt});
  stream.on('frame', f => {
    switch(f.type) {
      case 'narrative': ui.appendText(f.payload); break;
      case 'action_call': ui.showToolSpinner(f.payload.tool); break;
      case 'tool_patch': state = mergePatch(state, f.payload); break;
      case 'commit': state = f.payload; ui.replaceWithFinal(state); break;
    }
  });
  // helpers
  stream.on('speculative', meta => ui.decorateSpeculative(meta));
  await stream.commitPromise(); // resolves on commit or terminal error
- Hedging helpers: client SDK exposes an opt-in helper that, on receiving an action_call frame, can attempt a small local fallback (developer provided) and mark it as speculative. When server tool_patch arrives, SDK automatically swaps in authoritative content or keeps local if the policy allows.
- Resume support: SDK stores resume_tokens and can call client.resume({resume_token}) to continue partial sessions after transient disconnects. Resume semantics intentionally limited to frame boundaries (no token-level replay).

Operational considerations
- Cost: small incremental bandwidth for speculative frames and resume tokens; design frames to be compact to limit token overhead.
- Routing: tool hedging increases tool request counts (speculative fallbacks are client-local); server-side hedging is primarily routing-based (fast-path vs. durable tool). Build dashboards that surface tool invocation rates and speculative reconcile rates.
- Backwards compatibility: existing streaming clients receive frames as extended SSE events; old clients will ignore new fields and continue to receive narrative tokens as before.

Telemetry & observability
- Events to emit per session: frame_emitted, action_call_emitted, speculative_emitted, tool_request_sent, tool_result_received, speculative_reconciled, commit_emitted.
- Aggregates to track: speculative reconciliation success rate, mean time from action_call to tool_patch, resume token reuse rate, client-side hedging adoption.

Rollout plan (phased)
1) Internal alpha (2 weeks): design SDK API, wireframe UI patterns, run internal prompts to validate schema tags.
2) Private beta (6 weeks): enable for 3 power customers with instrumented SDK; collect reconciliation metrics and golden prompt parse tests.
3) Public opt-in (4 weeks): GA toggle for Hosted API customers, default off. Provide migration guide and example UIs.
4) Default on for new streaming models after performance validation (Q2).

Safety and failure modes
- Speculative frames must be clearly marked to avoid leaking incorrect assertions as facts. SDK will surface speculative frames with lower visual weight.
- Merge conflicts: when both client speculative local patch and server tool_patch modify same field, server wins by default; provide configurable merge policies in Dedicated/Private.

Open questions
- Hedging policy thresholds: what confidence / time windows should trigger speculative emission? (ops + research tuning needed)
- How to represent complex patch diffs compactly yet intelligible to clients? JSON Patch vs. small custom key-value patches?
- Resume token TTL and statefulness: server memory vs. cheap durable store (pricing implications).

Next steps & ask
- Engineering: feasibility spike to implement frame envelopes in streaming runtime (2 sprints).
- Research: run experiments on model behavior for speculative fallback phrasing and schema tag accuracy (2-3 weeks).
- Design: produce 2 reference client UI mocks (desktop and mobile) showing speculative UX and reconciliation flows.
- PM: land beta customers and draft migration docs.

Appendix: quick example session (SSE pseudo)
--event: frame
data: {"seq":1, "type":"narrative", "payload":"Hello — I can help with that.\n"}
--event: frame
data: {"seq":2, "type":"action_call", "payload":{"tool":"kb.fetch","args":{"query":"privacy policy refund"}}, "resume_token":"r_abc123"}
// SDK shows a spinner for kb.fetch and optionally emits a speculative frame: 
--event: frame
data: {"seq":3, "type":"narrative", "payload":"In short: refunds processed within 30 days. (speculative)", "speculative": true, "schema_tag":"summary.v1"}
// tool result arrives 
--event: frame
data: {"seq":4, "type":"tool_patch", "payload":{"refund_window_days":30}, "resume_token":"r_abc123"}
--event: frame
data: {"seq":5, "type":"commit", "payload":{"answer":"Refunds are processed within 30 days.", "refund_window_days":30}, "schema_tag":"final.v1"}

Notes to reviewers: aim to focus feedback on the tradeoffs of speculative emissions and the minimal SDK surface. We intentionally keep resume semantics coarse to limit server-side state and reduce complexity for initial rollout.
